newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH BONDS DOWN, NEGATIVE OUTLOOK AFTER US FALL.
newsitem.headline: DANISH BONDS DOWN, NEGATIVE OUTLOOK AFTER US FALL.

text.p: Danish bond prices were lower in mid-morning trade on Wednesday, hit by overnight Wall Street falls, with dealers expecting a negative mood to prevail ahead of the afternoon's U.S. June retail sales data.
"The general market undertone is negative after the U.S. falls. Focus is on the American figures," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded 0.24 point down on Tuesday's close at 112.41, yielding 6.08 percent , at 0835 GMT. The seven percent 2007 paper, due to be benchmark on September 1, was 0.25 point lower at 105.30, with yield at 6.27 percent.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point from Tuesday's close to 58 bps.
The crown traded at 3.8102 per mark, weakening from 3.8085.
